'Cast out devils' is one of the commonest phrases in the synoptic gospels and appears in a dozen KJV verses across Matthew, Mark and Luke; no one of them can be identified as the source of Mosiah 3:6, and the Book of Mormon's gloss — 'or the evil spirits which dwelleth in the hearts of the children of men' — is not from any of them. The Book of Mormon's 'shall say that he hath a Devil' is the charge in general, not any one occurrence of it. The verse's identifiable sources are John 1:11 and the synoptic passion prediction, both catalogued at the link; this phrase is real KJV contact that cannot be keyed to a verse.

“stiffnecked” occurs in nine KJV verses, six of them of Israel at Sinai and in Deuteronomy, and the phrase 'a stiffnecked people' in five. Ephesians 4:22-24 makes the same exhortation as Colossians 3:9-12 and is the passage more often quoted for it, so it is the natural rival here.
